headline: Brazil had its worst day since 2020, though US listed Brazil names closed well off their premarket lows; an AI rally after Anthropic's IPO filing lifted the S&P 500 0.7%, and the Fed meeting starts today with SK hynix reporting tonight.
summary: The dashboard now has Monday Oct 26 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-26). Brazil's Ibovespa fell 13.88% to 176,608.23 and the dollar rose 8.21% to R$5.4027, its biggest daily gain since 1999 (InfoMoney, Exame); in New York EWZ closed down 19.8% at 34.15 and NU down 17.0% at 12.59, below the 13.10 line where the dashboard says its long term case breaks. The S&P 500 rose 0.70% to 7,676.77 as chip stocks rallied after Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq, and the KOSPI followed with a 3.09% gain today (Zacks via Yahoo, Digital Today). Brent traded near $114.68 early Tuesday as Saudi, Pakistani, Turkish and Iranian officials agreed to keep talking; yesterday's 'down about 2%' was an intraday print, and Monday ended only slightly lower. PayPal beat on profit and raised its full year outlook but missed on revenue, and its verdict slipped to 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' on Monday's close. No new swing, put or PMCC idea; the Fed decides Wednesday at 2pm ET.

regime.why: US stocks rose and the VIX fell 5.45% to 18.39 Monday, but the gains rest on new AI money coming to market: Meta's upsized stock sale and an Anthropic IPO that reports put near $100 billion. Brazil showed how hard a crowded bet can break, and the Fed is expected to hold Wednesday with a December hike still in play.

signals.title: Brazil's selloff held at the close: Ibovespa -13.88%, EWZ -19.8%, and NU closed below the line where its long term case breaks
signals.since_yesterday: Monday's closes are in. US listed Brazil names closed well off their premarket lows, but NU finished at 12.59, under its 13.10 'thesis broken' line, and its verdict changed from 'Buy zone now' to Wait.
signals.what_happened: The Ibovespa fell 13.88% to 176,608.23 on Oct 26, its biggest one day loss since March 2020, after the first circuit breaker since then; the dollar rose 8.21% to R$5.4027 after touching R$5.6048 (InfoMoney, Exame). InfoMoney says the market began pricing a Selic hike in November. US listed closes on Oct 26 (dashboard): EWZ 34.15, down 19.8%; NU 12.59, down 17.0%; ITUB 7.70, down 20.4%; BBD 2.93, down 28.0%; PBR 22.50, down 14.0%; MELI 1668.72, down 7.8%. So the premarket drop mostly held for the banks and BBD, while EWZ closed 7.3% above its 31.83 premarket print and NU 8.8% above 11.57 (my calculation). Volume was heavy: NU traded 4.17 times its 50 day average and EWZ 7.11 times. On the vote: one report says Flavio Bolsonaro dropped his annulment request a day after making it and will pursue a separate abuse of power case (SBS); his Liberal Party said it accepts the official count (TRT World), though TRT says he still disputes it, so the reports conflict. UBS sees Brazilian stocks falling another 10% to 15% (one report, Yahoo Finance). Argentine stocks fell 3.0% Monday as the peso slid (Rio Times).
signals.so_what: Heavy volume on a down day is distribution, not a flush that is over. The closes tell the story: the dollar and the banks did not bounce, because a Selic hike now looks likely when the central bank meets Nov 3 to 4, and higher rates hit lenders twice, through funding costs and loan losses. MELI fell least because it earns across Latin America, not only in Brazil. If Flavio really has stepped back from annulment, the political tail risk shrinks, but the budget question that drove the selloff does not. What would make this wrong: a credible spending pledge from Lula's team, or the central bank holding rates while the real stabilizes.
signals.for_you: Long term: NU is now Wait at 12.59, 10.6% under its 14.08 to 15.00 zone and 3.9% under the 13.10 line the dashboard calls 'thesis broken' (my calculation). Do not buy it; the case needs a rethink after the Nov 3 to 4 rate decision and its next report. Puts: if you sold the Setups scanner's EWZ Nov 20 $37 put, EWZ closed 7.7% below the strike (my calculation). EWZ has no verdict, so the roll rule says no roll; the choice is to keep it and accept shares at 37 or buy it back. No Brazil swings or new puts.

signals.title: Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq and chips rallied, Meta priced its upsized stock sale at $625, and the KOSPI jumped 3.09%
signals.what_happened: Anthropic publicly filed an S-1 on Oct 26 to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as ANT, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley; the filing does not yet give a share count, price range or date (SEC, Investing.com). Press reports put the raise near $100 billion at a $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion valuation, which is not confirmed by the filing, and one outlet reports an $80.7 billion net loss and more than $500 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments (IBTimes). The S&P 500 rose 0.70% to 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq 0.82% to 26,169.38, with chips leading (Zacks via Yahoo, CNBC); on the dashboard NVDA rose 2.4%, AMD 2.8% and AVGO 2.3%. Meta priced its offerings at $625 a share for common stock and $50 per depositary share for the mandatory convertible preferred, upsizing the common to $25 billion, for up to $37.5 billion in total (SEC filing); Nvidia agreed to buy $3 billion of the stock as part of a wider AI partnership (Quartz). Meta closed at 630.56, down 1.9%. In Seoul the KOSPI rose 3.09% to 5,638.34 today, SK hynix up 5.18% to 1,341,000 won and Samsung up 4.23% to 222,000 won, as foreigners bought a net 592.9 billion won (Digital Today). Neoclouds steadied after Sunday's Musk warning: CRWV closed up 1.8% at 55.19 and NBIS down 3.4% at 153.27 (dashboard).
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the AI build now runs on new stock. Meta's $37.5 billion, a possible $60 billion Meta share program in 2027 and an Anthropic IPO near $100 billion would add a large supply of AI shares in a few months, and the buyers have to sell something else to pay for them. In the short run the cash goes straight to chip, memory and server makers, which is why NVDA, SK hynix and Samsung rallied. The second order risk is the loop: Nvidia is helping fund one of its biggest customers. Third order: when the best informed buyers of AI, the companies themselves, choose to sell stock, it tells you they think prices are rich. What would make this wrong: strong cloud growth and capex guides from Alphabet and Microsoft on Wednesday.
signals.for_you: No chip swings or puts before Wednesday night. NVDA (216.00) and AMD (531.28) are 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'; NVDA's sellers still lead slightly (up/down 0.97), while AMD's buyers lead (1.21) but it is down 15.8% in a month. META is Wait at 630.56, 31% above the top of its fair value range (dashboard). NBIS stays 'Accumulate on pullback' and CRWV has too little data.

signals.title: AI hardware results: Celestica and Cadence beat and raised, Amkor missed; PayPal beat on profit, missed on revenue
signals.since_yesterday: The numbers are out for the four reports Monday's brief flagged, plus PayPal, Boeing and Novartis this morning.
signals.what_happened: Celestica: revenue $5.83 billion, up 83%, adjusted EPS $3.30 against $2.99 expected; it raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $21.0 billion from $20.5 billion and EPS to $11.55 from $11.30, but cut free cash flow guidance to $460 million from $600 million. CLS closed at 246.65, down 5.1%, then rose about 9% after hours to about 268.99 (MoneyCheck; Investing.com said about 9.7%). Cadence: revenue $1.633 billion, non-GAAP EPS $2.11, 2026 EPS guide raised to $8.37 to $8.43, backlog $8.2 billion and $2.5 billion more for buybacks (SEC filing); CDNS closed at 322.17, up 1.8%, and Investing.com had it 2.15% higher after hours, while Yahoo said flat. Amkor: sales $1.991 billion, flat from a year ago and below forecasts, EPS $0.76; Q4 guide $1.9 to $2.0 billion with EPS $0.65 to $0.75 (SEC filing); AMKR closed at 36.81, down 6.3%, and after hours reports conflict. Rambus: record revenue $218.3 million, up 22%, non-GAAP EPS $0.84 (company release). This morning PayPal reported adjusted EPS $1.45 against $1.31 expected but revenue of $8.58 billion against $8.71 billion, and raised its 2026 EPS guide to $5.60 from $5.38; premarket moves ranged from down 0.3% to down 2% at $53.90 (Investing.com, Benzinga). Boeing's revenue of $24.19 billion beat $23.84 billion expected, with a loss of 26 cents a share (TheStreet). Visa reports after the close.
signals.so_what: The split is the message: companies tied to AI data center builds (Celestica's servers and switches, Cadence's chip design software, Rambus's memory chips) are growing fast, while Amkor, which packages chips for phones as well as AI, is flat. Celestica also shows the cost of growth: more sales but less free cash, because it has to fund inventory and capacity for customers. For PayPal, profit is rising from cost cuts while revenue lags, which is a turnaround, not growth.
signals.for_you: No action. CLS is Wait at 246.65 (zone 317.34 to 342.91) and AMKR is Wait at 36.81 with sellers well ahead (up/down 0.54); a one night pop does not change a downtrend. CDNS and RMBS are not rated on the dashboard. PYPL: the price is in its 48.29 to 57.35 zone, but sellers lead (0.94) and the 200 day average is falling, so it is a watch, not a buy; no put until the verdict returns to 'Buy zone now'.

signals.title: Oil is drifting lower on Tehran talks, not falling hard; XOM and CVX swings hit their 2R targets
signals.since_yesterday: A correction and two closed trades: Monday's 'Brent down about 2% to $114.50' was an early print, Bloomberg had Brent near $116 later, and it slipped to about $114.68 early Tuesday. The scorecard graded the XOM and CVX swings as 2R wins on Oct 26.
signals.what_happened: Saudi, Turkish, Pakistani and Iranian officials agreed after Monday's Tehran meeting to keep talking, and one report says Iran would reopen Hormuz within seven days if its conditions are met (Free Press Journal). Brent traded near $114.68 early Tuesday, down for a second session (FinanceFeeds), with WTI near $101 (Voice of Emirates). Against that, Iran's Revolutionary Guard declared the strait closed on Oct 26 and said ships must use its approved northern corridor, reported by one outlet citing Tasnim (House of Saud), and Houthi strikes on Saudi pumping stations are still claimed. On the dashboard XOM closed at 184.54 and CVX at 232.01; the scorecard closed both swings as wins at their 2R targets (183.99 and 233.79) on Oct 26.
signals.so_what: The market is trading the talks, not the threats: a closed strait plus only a slow drift lower means traders think a deal is more likely than not. That keeps inflation pressure in Thursday's PCE but not as bad as a spike. Producers near 52 week highs have little left to gain from more fear and a lot to lose from a deal.
signals.for_you: Swings: the XOM and CVX plans hit 2R, so by the rules those trades are done; if you still hold them, take profits or trail a stop, because both report Oct 30. COP (151.37, stop 135.75) and EOG (163.68, stop 147.98) are open with buyers leading (up/down 1.13 and 1.43). No new energy swings or puts into the reports. DAL is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (79.16, up/down 0.99): a close with buyers in charge could make it ready.

signals.title: A judge let Lilly keep its Zepbound versus Wegovy ads, a small win in the obesity price war
signals.what_happened: On Oct 26 US District Judge Zahid Quraishi refused Novo Nordisk's request to block Eli Lilly's ads claiming Zepbound beats Wegovy and Mounjaro beats Ozempic, saying Novo had not shown irreparable harm; Novo's July lawsuit continues (Reuters via Investing.com, Bloomberg). Separately, a regulatory roundup reports FDA approved at home under the skin induction dosing for AbbVie's Skyrizi in Crohn's disease (The Pharma Letter, headline only).
signals.so_what: In a market that Bloomberg Intelligence sizes at $120 billion a year by 2030, ads that compare drugs head to head shape what patients ask for and what insurers cover. Lilly already leads in sales, so the ruling protects its momentum. For clinicians, at home induction for a biologic like Skyrizi cuts infusion center visits, which helps patients and hurts infusion volumes.
signals.for_you: No action. LLY is 'Accumulate on pullback' at 1279.14, about 4.5% above the top of its zone (my calculation); NVO has too little data. PFE, on the GLP-1 map, is newly 'Buy zone now' at 29.79 but reports Nov 3, so wait for the report.

cycle.big_cycle: Technology: AI spending now leans on public stock markets. Internal order: Brazil's loser has stepped back from annulment in one report but not in another, and the US votes Nov 3. External order: talks continue in Tehran while Iran's Guard calls Hormuz closed.
tailwinds: Fresh capital for AI keeps orders flowing to chip, memory and server makers in the near term.

headwinds: A wave of new AI stock supply competes for the same buyers.
Brazil's crash and a likely Selic hike show how fast crowded emerging market bets can break.

history.when: 1999 to March 2000, the dot com IPO wave
history.what: 476 US companies went public in 1999, raising $36.94 billion with an average first day gain of 71% (Ritter). The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, shortly after the issuance peak.
history.lesson: When companies rush to sell stock, they are telling you prices are high. One Anthropic deal near $100 billion would be about 2.7 times all 1999 IPO proceeds (my calculation, not adjusted for inflation).

source.title: IPO statistics: 1999 count, proceeds and first day returns (Jay Ritter, University of Florida)

cycle.differences: In 1999 most new issuers had little revenue; today's AI sellers have real and fast growing sales, but also huge losses and spending commitments. Rates are also far higher than in 1999, which makes paying up for distant profits harder.
cycle.for_you: Swing: take profits on XOM and CVX by the plan; no new trades before the Fed and big tech. Puts: none; no live quote passes the rules today. Long term: buy only names in 'Buy zone now' that are not reporting this week; NU is out.

principle.text: To make money in markets you have to think independently and bet against the consensus, and be right (paraphrased from Principles).
principle.applied: The consensus is lining up to buy the biggest AI stock sales on record. Thinking independently here means asking why the best informed holders are selling, and waiting for prices that pay you for that risk.
